newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says grants natural gas transport permit.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says grants natural gas transport permit.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said on Wednesday it had issued a natural gas transportation permit to Gasoductos de Chihuahua.
The permit will allow the company to transport natural gas to the federal government's Samalayuca thermo-electric plants in the northern state of Chihuahua.
Gasoductos de Chihuahua is a subsidiary of Pemex Gas y Petroquimica Basica, El Paso Natural Gas Co, and El Paso Energy International Co.
Pemex Gas y Petroquimica Basica is a subsidiary of state-owned Petroleos Mexicanos, and owns 50 percent of Gasoductos de Chihuahua.
El Paso Natural Gas Co has 40 percent, and El Paso Energy International Co the remaining 10 percent.
With the permit the company will be able to construct, operate and maintain a 38-kilometer long natural gas pipe from the U.S.-Mexican border at San Isidro to Samalayuca.
Total capacity will be 219 million cubic feet per day.
The investment costs will be $18.2 million, the CRE said in a statement.
